purpose: Canonical contracts for the 45 child-agent roles. These definitions describe ownership and expected evidence; they do not claim an LLM or external tool has executed a role.

operations: Break the requested outcome into ordered tasks.
A task graph with owners, dependencies, and measurable acceptance criteria.
Order eligible tasks under the single-active-site lock.
A valid execution order with no concurrent site claims.
Check site authorization and task constraints before work.
Explicit pass/block decision with the policy checks recorded.
Validate persisted runtime state and transition consistency.
State snapshot with no conflicting active-site or invalid transition.
Summarize verified progress and blockers for the manager.
Report cites runtime events or artifacts and distinguishes unknowns.
research: Identify sources explicitly authorized for the active site.
Source list with URLs, access scope, and relevance notes.
Prioritized findings with rationale and source references.
Assess supported changes or patterns over time.
Time-bounded observations with dates and evidence.
media: Validate the configured source and allowed usage.
Source authorization result and source provenance.
Prepare permitted assets for site use.
Asset paths, format checks, and transformation notes.
Write descriptive metadata and alt text.
Metadata tied to the actual asset and page context.
Check documented rights and usage constraints.
Rights decision with evidence; block if unclear.
Review assets for quality and policy compliance.
Review result with asset references and required fixes.
publishing: Prepare content changes within the approved scope.
Changed-file list and content acceptance checks.
Prepare a release candidate from approved changes.
Release summary, commit reference, and rollback point.
Verify deployment workflow and target status.
Workflow run URL/status or explicit not-verified result.
Prepare or execute an authorized rollback plan.
Target commit and rollback verification; no destructive action without authorization.
seo: Research relevant search intent from authorized sources.
Keyword groups with intent and evidence/source notes.
Validate titles, descriptions, canonical, and indexing directives.
Per-URL metadata checklist and detected issues.
Check internal links and navigation paths.
Broken-link report and proposed link changes.
Validate sitemap coverage and URL consistency.
Sitemap parse result and URL coverage findings.
Assess crawl/indexing signals without claiming guaranteed indexing.
quality: Test core user-facing flows against acceptance criteria.
Reproducible test cases and pass/fail results.
Check layout, interaction, and responsive behavior.
Check technical SEO requirements for changed pages.
Measured metrics, test conditions, and thresholds.
Aggregate evidence and decide whether release criteria pass.
Release decision with blockers; never infer success from missing evidence.
diagnostics: Inspect available logs for actionable failure signals.
Relevant log excerpts, timestamps, and suspected failure stage.
Create a minimal reproducible case for a reported issue.
Steps, expected/actual behavior, and reproduction result.
Separate root cause from symptoms using evidence.
Ranked causes with supporting and contradicting evidence.
Define checks that prevent the issue returning.
Regression test list mapped to the defect.
Reviewed cause, confidence, and remaining unknowns.
repair: Propose the smallest safe fix within authorized files.
Patch diff and rationale; no unapproved scope expansion.
Run relevant checks against the proposed fix.
Exact commands/checks and results, including failures.
Review the change for access-control and secret-handling risks.
Security findings and explicit pass/block result.
Define recovery steps before risky release changes.
Known-good reference and tested or clearly untested rollback steps.
Review fix quality and required regression evidence.
Acceptance decision linked to patch and test evidence.
innovation: Collect evidence for a proposed product or site idea.
Evidence-backed problem statement and source notes.
Score demand, feasibility, and risks transparently.
Scoring rubric, assumptions, and uncertainty notes.
Scope, deliverables, acceptance criteria, and dependencies.
Track an approved experiment and its measurements.
Experiment record with baseline, observation window, and results.
Review whether evidence supports continuing the idea.

integration_status.note: A role must only be marked WORKING or COMPLETED after its runtime adapter actually executes and records evidence.
